subject: Audit sampling windows vs BYOK retention — prioritization & risk alignment
messages:
From: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@acmehealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.example.com
Cc: acme-procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-03-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Audit logs sampling window + BYOK retention compatibility

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looks promising. We ran the internal checklist with our compliance team and surfaced two items we need aligned before procurement can proceed:

1) Audit sampling windows: We need to export high-fidelity audit streams for 90-day sampling windows but only store long-term aggregates in Redacted form. We asked whether Redwood can support both live streaming of raw events to our SIEM while simultaneously applying a short-term windowed retention for raw tokens.

2) BYOK retention carveouts: Because we manage keys in our HSM, we need confirmation that short-term audit artifacts (for sampling) can be exported without creating a long-term BYOK retention footprint in Redwood. If keys are rotated or removed, sample exports must still be verifiable.

Can your team outline acceptable approaches and timeline? Procurement would like a short scope note for our SOC 2 review by 3/21.

Attachments: audit_log_sample_schema.csv (sample CSV with columns we need), BYOK_requirements.docx (high level, from our infosec).

Appreciate a quick triage — Sara
Acme Health — Compliance
From: olga.petrov@redwood.example.com
To: sara.dunne@acmehealth.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com, ben.carter@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-03-14T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit logs sampling window + BYOK retention compatibility

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. I pulled Ben (security eng) and Grace (product) in so we can give concrete options. High-level responses first:

- Yes, we can stream raw audit events in real time to a customer-managed SIEM (Kafka/HTTP). That stream is independent of our internal retention policies.
- For short-term sampling we can support a 90-day raw-event buffer that is customer-exportable; after that a redacted aggregate is stored long-term.
- BYOK: we can provide signed export bundles that are verifiable by your HSM after key rotation/removal. There are two implementation paths (see details below).

Quick ask from our side: can you confirm whether the exported sample artifacts need to be re-ingestable into Acme's SIEM, or if a verifiable, append-only bundle is sufficient? That will change the API contract.

I'll summarize options in a follow-up within 24 hours and propose a timeline for the SOC 2 note.

— Olga
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.example.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.example.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-03-14T15:20:00Z
Subject: RE: Audit logs sampling window + BYOK retention compatibility

Folks — quick tech breakout so we can give Sara concrete options. Two feasible approaches (tradeoffs):

Option A — Streaming + ephemeral buffer
- Stream raw audit events to Acme in real time (HTTPS/Kafka).
- Keep a 90-day ephemeral raw buffer in Redwood (encrypted with customer key) strictly for exports.
- After 90 days, purge raw events and retain redacted aggregates (non-reversible) for compliance.
- Pros: minimal long-term BYOK footprint, simple export semantics.
- Cons: requires a short-lived key escrow or signing token at export time to allow verification post-rotation.

Option B — Signed export bundles (no raw buffer required)
- Create signed, chunked export bundles on demand using customer public key.
- Bundles contain raw events for requested windows and are signed by Redwood using a time-stamped signature which Acme verifies against their key material.
- Pros: no raw storage beyond immediate processing; compatible with strict BYOK policies.
- Cons: higher CPU cost for signing and potentially slower exports for large windows.

Questions for product: do we have throughput constraints that make Option B impractical for 90-day exports at Acme scale? Grace — can you advise on expected export perf and whether we should recommend a limited window size per export?

Ben
Senior Security Engineer
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.example.com, olga.petrov@redwood.example.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-03-15T10:44:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit logs sampling window + BYOK retention compatibility

Ben, brief product perspective and roadmap asks:

- Current export pipeline comfortably handles up to 30 days raw-export at scale with bounded latency; 90-day exports are supported but may need batching to avoid impacting serving SLOs during peak.
- Implementing signed export bundles (Option B) is a medium-priority engineering workstream — estimate 6–8 weeks for a hardened rollout (includes e2e verification tests and key rotation flows).
- Ephemeral 90-day buffer (Option A) is lower engineering complexity but requires clear policy around key escrow/signing tokens. If Acme is comfortable with a short-lived token model, we can deliver a 90-day buffer in ~3–4 weeks with a documented ops runbook.

Action items I recommend we propose to Acme:
1) Immediate: proof-of-concept signed bundle for a 7-day window (2 weeks to deliver).
2) Short-term: enable ephemeral 90-day buffer behind a procurement feature flag (3–4 weeks) so they can meet SOC2 review timelines.
3) Roadmap: prioritize signed-bundle native flow (6–8 weeks).

I also flagged potential product constraints: long-running 90-day exports should be rate-limited per account to protect multi-tenant throughput. We should propose explicit limits in the SOC2 note.

Grace
Product Manager, Observability
From: olga.petrov@redwood.example.com
To: sara.dunne@acmehealth.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.example.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com, laura.bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-03-16T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit logs sampling window + BYOK retention compatibility — proposed plan and timeline

Sara — quick follow-up with a proposed path to meet your SOC2 review by 2028-03-21:

Proposed deliverables and timeline:
- By 2028-03-21: short scope note + explicit export limits for your SOC2 packet (deliverable: PDF redline). Owner: Olga.
- By 2028-03-28: PoC signed export bundle for a 7-day window (deliverable: signed-bundle.tar.gz + verification script). Owner: Ben (engineering).
- By 2028-04-11: Ephemeral 90-day buffer behind feature flag (deliverable: ops runbook + enable guide + sample export). Owner: Grace (product + infra).

Notes and clarifications:
- For the SOC2 scope note we will call out both Option A (ephemeral buffer) and Option B (signed bundles) as supported patterns and recommend Option A short-term to meet procurement timelines.
- Exports will be rate-limited: default 1TB/day per account for long-window exports; we can increase with a committed throughput contract (Dedicated).
- All exported artifacts will be digitally signed and include a manifest for validation. If you need re-ingest, we can add S3-compatible object layout.

Attachments: proposal-redline-0308.pdf (initial scope note).

Please confirm if this plan works for Acme and whether the 1TB/day default export limit is acceptable. If so, I will package the SOC2 packet and send to procurement.

Thanks — Olga
From: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@acmehealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.example.com
Cc: acme-procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-03-16T18:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit logs sampling window + BYOK retention compatibility — proposed plan and timeline

Thanks, Olga — this is great and aligns with expectations. Procurement wants the signed-bundle PoC included in the SOC2 packet if possible, but 7-day PoC is fine. The 1TB/day default looks conservative; we should be able to stay under that initially.

Please proceed and send the SOC2 scope note; procurement will confirm contract language thereafter.

Sara
